commits: 7000fc48d567be16cd474ee06e908b9f85f96863 Hand Claude its prompt as a stream-json message and keep stdin open until the result
1.1.handover:
## What landed
One commit. `claude.Start` passes `--input-format stream-json`, creates an
`os.Pipe`, hands the read end to `harness.StartProc` as stdin, closes the
parent's copy of it, and writes the prompt as
`{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"..."}}\n`.
The write end lives in `session.stdin` (`*input`: mutex, `send(line)`,
idempotent `close()`). It is closed on `result`, on `Kill`, and by a defer in
`session.read` when output ends without a result.
`dev/fakeagent` as `claude` reads only the first line when argv carries
`--input-format stream-json`; otherwise it still reads to EOF (its own tests
pipe a raw prompt).
Tests added in `claude_test.go`: first stdin line, and `Wait` returning for a
fake that prints a result then waits for EOF, one that exits without a result,
and one killed.

## Landmark drift
None. `harness.StartProc` is unchanged; it already accepts an `io.Reader`, and
an `*os.File` goes straight to `cmd.Stdin`, so `Cmd.Wait` has no copy goroutine.

## Deviations from the work order
None.

## What the next session must know
- The prompt write in `Start` is synchronous. A pipe holds 64 KB, so a larger
  prompt blocks until the child reads. A real claude reads; a context cancel or
  a crash fails the write (EPIPE). A test fake that never reads stdin is fine
  for small prompts only.
- A fake that neither prints a `result` nor exits keeps stdin open and hangs
  `Wait`, as the real claude would. Test fakes must exit or print a result.
- Later units should write via `s.stdin.send(line)` (one full line including
  `\n`); it errors with `os.ErrClosed` after close.
- `Kill` calls `proc.Kill()` first, then closes stdin, so a write blocked on a
  full pipe is released by the child's death rather than by the close.
- `codex` still uses `strings.NewReader`; untouched.

## Open problems
None. All checks and `go test ./...` were green.

commits: cea45339c84ddcdf2e670481672c21b8a16858de Ping a waiting Claude session before its five-minute cache expires
2.1.handover:
## What landed
One commit. New `internal/harness/claude/warm.go`: a `warmer` per session with
the clock, pending main-thread calls (deadline or zero), pings since the last
real request, last main-thread context size, outstanding ping. `run()` is a
goroutine started in `Start`; `read()` feeds it (`call`, `results`, `usage`,
`answered`) and `defer s.endWarming()` joins it and turns a stop into
`drift.Missing("cache warming stopped: ...")` before `done` closes.
`Start` uses `StartProcWithEnv` with `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=5m`.
`control_response` lines are read. `harness.Outcome` gained `Pings` and
`PingTokens` (cache-read estimate only). Tests in `warm_test.go`.

## Landmark drift
None.

## Deviations from the work order
- Tuning values are package vars in `warm.go` (`pingAfter`, `deadlineMargin`,
  `pingCap`, `answerWait`, `cacheTTL`) plus the tool limits
  (`defaultBashTimeout`, `maxBashTimeout`, `defaultMonitorTimeout`,
  `maxMonitorTimeout`), so tests shrink the deadline arithmetic too.
- The subagent-clock test drives `session.assistant`/`toolResults` directly
  rather than through a fake process: timing through a process cannot show a
  clock that did not move deterministically.
- Several pending calls with one unknown deadline count as unknown (the latest
  of a set containing infinity).

## What the next session must know
- Warming is always on; there is no switch yet. 2.2 must add the `cache = "1h"`
  opt-out: skip the TTL env var (or set `1h`) and do not start/finish the
  warmer (`newWarmer`/`run` in `Start`; `finish` is called from `read` and
  closes `quit`, so it must not run on a warmer whose `run` never started).
- `BASH_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS`/`BASH_MAX_TIMEOUT_MS` are read from ploopy's own
  environment when the warmer is created (the child inherits it).
- A ping write error (child gone) ends warming silently, with counts rolled
  back; only error/synthetic/missing answers leave a note.
- `Outcome.Pings`/`PingTokens` are filled in `Wait`; nothing consumes them yet
  (2.3 books them). Other adapters leave them zero.
- Test fake: `warmingClaude` in `warm_test.go` reads stdin by line, has
  `reply ok|error|synthetic|silent`, and records unread stdin at exit.

## Open problems
None. Build, vet, gofmt and `go test ./...` green; the claude package also
passed `-race -count=5`.

commits: dc2d31dfd5228809af1cc5d9ea7ba4dac7a8db65 Let [agents.claude] cache = "1h" opt a repository out of cache warming
2.2.handover:
## What landed
One commit. `config.Agent.Cache` (`cache` key); `Load` refuses any value but
`warm`/`1h` under `[agents.claude]` and any `cache` under another agent, naming
`agents.<name>.cache`. `allHarnesses` copies it to `claude.Harness.Cache`.
`Start` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PROMPT_CACHE_TTL=1h` and builds no warmer when it is
`1h` (`CacheHour`; `CacheWarm` and empty mean warm). README and
`skills/ploopy/SKILL.md` describe the key.

## Landmark drift
None.

## Deviations from the work order
- A nil `*warmer` means warming off: every warmer method returns at once on nil,
  so `read`, `Wait` and `endWarming` needed no branches.
- `config` uses the literals `"warm"`/`"1h"` rather than importing the adapter.

## What the next session must know
- `Outcome.Pings`/`PingTokens` are zero under `1h`, as for the other adapters.
- Tests: config (`TestClaudeCacheLoads`, bad values in
  `TestInvalidAgentPreferencesAreRefused`); adapter
  `TestTheHourCacheSetsItAndSendsNoPing` (a call the default would ping, no
  request on stdin, TTL env `1h`).

## Open problems
None. Build, vet, gofmt, `go test ./...` green; claude and config packages
pass `-race -count=3`.

commits: ecfcfec7673004c4eba8c68c40716e7eed776bc5 Book keep-warm pings in the stats log, history and report
2.3.handover:
## What landed
One commit. `stats.Record` and `history.Record` gain `Pings` (`pings`) and
`PingTokens` (`ping_tokens`, pointer), both omitted when zero. `accountSession`
copies them from `harness.Outcome` for every role. The report prints a `Pings`
line after `Tokens`: count, estimated read tokens, marked "estimated, not in the
totals above". The line is built from the log's session records only.

## Landmark drift
None.

## Deviations from the work order
None.

## What the next session must know
- Pings are not in `spent`, the unit's state entry, the run's `stats.Run` or the
  run record: the state format is frozen, so the report shows them only when a
  stats log exists (nothing is said without one).
- Tests: loop `TestPingsAreBookedApartFromReportedTokens` (log, history, state
  tokens unchanged); stats `TestThePingsAreShownApartAndLeaveTheCacheShareAlone`,
  `TestARecordWithoutPingsSerializesAsBefore`.
- README/skills did not describe the report's token lines, so no doc changed.

## Open problems
None. Build, vet, gofmt and `go test ./...` green.
